entries.title: CLI update: ad-client-context

ai.title: Terminal detection expanded with Zed, Tabby, Mintty, Konsole, GNOME
ai.summary: The CLI's ad client context now classifies additional Linux and Windows terminals by reading their environment variables (KONSOLE_VERSION, GNOME_TERMINAL_SCREEN, VTE_VERSION, XTERM_VERSION, WT_SESSION, GHOSTTY_RESOURCES_DIR, ZED_TERM), and the common type vocabulary was extended to accept the new terminal and install-method enums. The detection is additive: a new out-of-vocabulary value drops the whole context rather than the single field, so clients and servers must both speak the new values, per a newly added warning in the schema file. A related refactor in ad-signals.ts replaced the raw-text extractor failedToolOutputText with shellFailureClassOf, which returns a classified error class instead of text, and resets lastErrorClass to 'none' on each turn start so stale errors do not ride later turns.
ai.evidence: Three files changed: cli/src/ads/ad-client-context.ts adds terminal detection for zed, tabby, mintty, conemu, windows_console, gnome_terminal, konsole, vte, xterm, foot and konsole via new environment variable reads (KONSOLE_VERSION, KONSOLE_DBUS_SESSION, GNOME_TERMINAL_SCREEN, GNOME_TERMINAL_SERVICE, VTE_VERSION, XTERM_VERSION, WT_SESSION, GHOSTTY_RESOURCES_DIR, ZED_TERM); common/src/types/ad-client-context.ts adds the corresponding terminal enum values plus 'bunx' to INSTALL_METHODS and documents that vocabularies are additive-only (one out-of-range value drops the whole context); cli/src/ads/ad-signals.ts renames failedToolOutputText to shellFailureClassOf, which now returns an error class directly instead of raw text, and resets lastErrorClass to 'none' at each turn start.
ai.unknowns: The diff does not show whether the server-side ad routes (/api/v1/ads, /api/ads) have been updated to accept the new vocabulary values, only that the schema warns they must be before a client sends them.

changes.what: Expanded terminal detection to identify zed, tabby, mintty, conemu, windows_console, gnome_terminal, konsole, vte, xterm, and foot from their environment variables, and read real launcher paths via getCliEnv().CODEBUFF_IS_BINARY.
Added the new terminal enum values and 'bunx' to INSTALL_METHODS, and documented that vocabularies are additive-only with one out-of-range value dropping the whole context.
Replaced failedToolOutputText with shellFailureClassOf, which returns an error class directly instead of raw text, and reset lastErrorClass to 'none' at each turn start.

eli5.text: The assistant's terminal recognition got smarter so it can now tell you're using Zed, Tabby, Mintty, Konsole, GNOME Terminal or a plain Windows console instead of lumping you in with every other unknown terminal. This is an internal change for the engineering team's testing and tracking, so it does not change how the assistant codes or what features you see. If you use one of those terminals you will simply be correctly identified in the logs, but there is no visible change to your daily workflow.

facts: Everything the root may spawn: pickers and searchers for context, the worker for slices. The code-searcher is programmatic — a batch of ripgrep queries and no model call — so it needs no free-mode allowlist entry.

What a worker may not run of base3's own tools: the terminal, because verification is the root's, once, for every slice together, and a worker with a terminal runs the suite N times in parallel; and the todo list, which is the root's plan. Everything else base3 has, the worker has.

Deliberately short and mostly suggestions: the agent answers questions, explores as long as it needs to, and decides when to split. What it is told firmly is the one thing it would otherwise skip (spawning helpers in parallel) and the one failure the fan-out invites (incoherent slices).
Drop the web tools, as createBase3CliRoot does for the eval harness.

Neither arm may read the public repository under evaluation off the web: read_url is refused by the bench, and a search result quoting its current code is the answer key. Both arms lose the two tools together.

A worker must be pinned to its root's model or the session gate rejects it mid-run, so the worker id names the model. Which models run this harness is FREEBUFF_FAST_MODE_MODEL_IDS (common/src/constants/freebuff-model-ids.ts).

entries.title: CLI update: ad-engagement

ai.title: CLI ad engagement adds checkpoint and late-click merge records
ai.summary: The CLI ad engagement registry gains checkpoints and late-click merge handling in `cli/src/ads/ad-engagement.ts`: a live impression now emits a checkpoint via `checkpoint()` (the record so far, no exit) when a transcript card leaves the viewport after being seen, or after `ENGAGEMENT_CHECKPOINT_MS` of exposure, whichever comes first, and a redraw of an already-flushed impression gets a click-only tracker that sends only `{ impUrl, click }` plus `postClick` so a late click still reaches the original record without overwriting the first click's features (the count grows instead). The `PartnerAdRow` component in `cli/src/components/partner-ad-line.tsx` is newly wired through `useAdEngagement` with placement: 'pinned', so partner rows now participate in that same registry alongside `AdCard`, and `cli/src/utils/exit-cleanly.ts` calls `flushAdEngagementOnExit()` from the shared exit path so any record that survived on a transcript card is sent as `window_close` on quit. A new `AdEngagementPoster` in `use-ad-engagement.ts` sequences per-impression POSTs with the later write winning on the server merge, and `ENGAGEMENT_CHECKPOINT_MS = 120_000` plus `MAX_CLICK_MEMO = 256` are the two new constants that gate the checkpoint timer and the clicked-impression memo.
ai.evidence: In `cli/src/ads/ad-engagement.ts`, `createEngagementRegistry.create` builds a click-only tracker via `createEngagementTracker({ clickOnly: { priorClick: clicks.get(impUrl) } })` when `mount` lands on an Impression already in finished, and the click-only `flush` path emits a `{ v, impUrl, click }` merge record through `sendLateClick`; `ENGAGEMENT_CHECKPOINT_MS = 120_000` and `MAX_CLICK_MEMO = 256` bound the checkpoint timer and the clicked-impression memo respectively; in `cli/src/components/partner-ad-line.tsx` the new `PartnerAdRow` component calls `useAdEngagement(ad.impUrl, { placement: 'pinned', truncated: layoutTruncated([ [ad.title, getPartnerLineLayout(ad, width).title], ]) }) and wires onClick`/`onHover into that tracker; in cli/src/utils/exit-cleanly.ts`, `createExitCliCleanly` pushes `Promise.resolve().then(deps.flushAdEngagement) into the exit cleanup list and the singleton supplies flushAdEngagement: () => flushAdEngagementOnExit() which calls live?.closeAll('window_close') followed by poster.settle()`.
ai.unknowns: The diff does not show the server-side consumer of the checkpoint or click-only merge records, nor the rollout of the engagement POST endpoint changes.

eli5.text: When you see a partner ad row in the CLI, like the one above the input or inside the /review menu, the assistant now records whether you scrolled it out of view before the ad finished and whether you clicked it after its first report already went out. It also makes sure that late clicks still get added to the original ad's total rather than starting a new count. You will not notice a new UI, but partner ad impressions and clicks are now tracked more accurately, including when the session ends.

ai.summary: The module-level JSDoc in `common/src/util/utc-days.ts` was rewritten so the four shared helpers are described as a single source of truth for the rollup jobs and dashboards. No logic lines changed, only the comment text explaining the dedup rationale and half-open window-boundary math.
ai.evidence: Modified file `common/src/util/utc-days.ts` contains a JSDoc comment block that now states the helpers `shiftUtcDay`, `todayUtc`, `dayWindowBounds`, and `trailingUtcDays` were previously copied into four consumers and are consolidated here to prevent drift of the half-open window-boundary math.
ai.unknowns: The diff shows only the comment rewrite, so the actual consumer files that previously held copies are not verified by this change alone.

eli5.text: The engineers rewrote the written explanation that sits above a small set of shared helper functions used to count and label whole days in UTC time, so that everyone reading the code can see that these helpers are the single place the rollup jobs and the dashboards should look for them, instead of each team maintaining its own copy that could silently drift out of sync. This is an internal code-comment update that changes the words developers read, not the words you read in the app, so it has no effect on how Freebuff or Codebuff behave for anyone using them. You will not notice anything different, and no action is required from you.
